briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's 'Dirt-for-Flower' Fine Rattles Growers as National Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market absorbed its biggest-ever regulatory gut-punch this week: a $2 million fine and 20 revoked grower licenses after a Clare processor shipped dirt and mulch labeled as marijuana flower, even as the state's 24% wholesale tax pushes prices to the lowest in the nation and drives more closures. Nationally, psychedelics kept building momentum — Compass Pathways confirmed durable 26-week Phase 3 results for its depression therapy, Portland moved to deprioritize psilocybin enforcement, and a bipartisan congressional caucus pressed the FDA to speed reviews — while a federal appeals ruling continues to narrow cannabis's interstate-commerce prospects.

local.text: Michigan revokes 20 grower licenses, fines processor $2M for shipping dirt as 'flower' — The CRA shut down GP Holdings LLC (Millie Montana Industries) after finding packages manifested as marijuana flower actually contained dirt, mulch, shake, kief, and plant waste — the state's largest-ever cannabis fine.

Tax pressure keeps squeezing Detroit shops — Detroit dispensary owner Stuart Carter (Utopia Gardens) is among operators warning that the 24% wholesale tax is accelerating closures and layoffs across Michigan's cannabis market.

Menominee's dispensary-cap vote set for Nov. 3 — The ballot measure to raise the city's dispensary limit from nine to 13 licenses now has a confirmed election date, giving Upper Peninsula operators a concrete timeline for potential expansion.

Michigan cements status as the nation's cheapest legal weed — Oversupply has pushed average flower prices to roughly $60 an ounce, turning border towns like Monroe Township and New Buffalo into magnets for Ohio and Illinois shoppers chasing lower prices.

Fourth-quarter wholesale tax period begins — Oct. 1 marks the start of Q4 (Oct. 1–Dec. 31) under the 24% wholesale marihuana tax, with payments due Jan. 20, as Treasury guidance continues to evolve amid industry confusion over collection.

national.text: Compass Pathways confirms durable psilocybin benefit at six months — The second Phase 3 trial (COMP006) of COMP360 showed a well-tolerated safety profile and responses sustained roughly six months after treatment for depression, bolstering the case for a possible 2027 FDA filing.

Portland moves to deprioritize psilocybin enforcement — City councilors advanced a Psychedelic Health and Safety Code making police enforcement of personal natural-psychedelic use one of the city's lowest priorities, while leaving trafficking and impaired-driving laws untouched.

Johns Hopkins study: cannabis is the top self-care tool for PMS and PMDD — A survey of over 700 people found 30% used cannabis to manage premenstrual mood symptoms (51.5% among those with PMDD), in the first study to also track psychedelic use across the menstrual cycle.

Interstate cannabis commerce hopes keep dimming — An Oregon wholesaler dropped its lawsuit challenging the state's cannabis export ban, citing the Ninth Circuit's Peridot Tree ruling that the dormant Commerce Clause doesn't protect marijuana activity under federal prohibition.

Bipartisan caucus presses FDA to speed psychedelic therapy reviews — Reps. Lou Correa and Jack Bergman, co-chairs of the congressional PATH Caucus, led 30 members of Congress urging FDA Commissioner Makary to accelerate evaluation of psychedelic-assisted therapies for serious mental illness.
